name: $k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension
definition: For an integer $k\ge0$, the **$k$-Mistake Littlestone Dimension** $\mathrm{L}^{\mathrm{mist}}_k(\mathcal{H})$ is the supremum, over binary decision trees whose every branch disagrees with some hypothesis in $\mathcal{H}$ on at most $k$ queried labels, of the minimum branch length.
graph_summary: Supremum of the minimum branch length of a tree whose paths are realizable with at most $k$ mistakes.
origin_references: Introduced by Filmus, Hanneke, Mehalel, and Moran \cite{filmus2023randomized}.

monotonic.proof: Every tree whose branches are $k$-realizable by a subfamily is also $k$-realizable by the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: A $k$-shattered tree for a projection queries only retained coordinates; lifting each realizing projected hypothesis to an original hypothesis realizes the same branches with the same number of disagreements.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: If both one-coordinate conditioned branches have $k$-mistake trees of minimum lengths a and b, attach the two trees below a root querying that coordinate. The root label agrees with the corresponding conditioned class, so the resulting tree is $k$-shattered and has minimum branch length at least $1+\min\{a,b\}$.

strictly_monotonic.proof: The parameter is doubly monotonic; its value can be zero only for an empty or singleton class, and the tree-grafting argument proves strict c-monotonicity.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: This fails for the two constant hypotheses when $k=1$: each one-coordinate branch is a singleton of value 1, whereas the whole class has value $2k+1=3$, not the required $1+1=2$.
